acceptance: A red-first test through the loop coordinator: a fixture wave whose lanes write the same abnormal-event kind past the bound engages the brake mid-wave, and the pool launches no new lane.
A replay of the wave 185 signal log at stage shadow records a would-trip before 10:00Z.
On a trip, one blocker item is routed to the console and one signal names the fault class, the lanes and the evidence.
Waves 184 and earlier, replayed, do not trip on their normal signal volume.
fix: Design review first. Add an in-wave breaker in the loop coordinator that reads the signal center while the wave runs. It trips when one fault class recurs across lanes past a bound in a window (for example the same abnormal-event kind in 3 or more lanes, or the same failure fingerprint in 2 or more cycles), or when the wave is older than a bound with lanes live and no ship. On a trip it engages the loop-stop brake (the pool stops backfill through poolHalted), emits one signal that names the fault, the lanes and the evidence, and routes one blocker item to the console (ORCHESTRATOR_BLOCKER_ROUTED, which the console listener takes). Bounds live in failure_policy.thresholds. Start at stage shadow and record would-trip events, then flip to enforce on a verified record.
summary: Operator 2026-11-21: on consistent failure, pause all tasks and fix the blocking issue first. Today no breaker can see a fault that slows every lane. The zero-ship breaker counts whole waves in fleet mode and runs only at the wave boundary (go/cmd/evolve/cmd_loop_window.go, zeroShipHalt before the next wave), so a wave that keeps running is never counted. The pipeline-blocker breaker counts completed cycle failures. The system-failure halt needs a cycle to signal one. Wave 185 ran 5.5 hours with 8 lanes and 0 of 9 cycles shipped. In that time the host verification lock timed out 73 times (verify-single-flight-unavailable abnormal events, cycles 2582 to 2590), LOOP_ORCH_LANE_STALLED fired 9 times and the shadow fleet window voted to widen (LOOP_ORCH_HOST_PRESSURE cap 7 to 8, 13:55Z). No signal fed a brake, and the operator engaged it by hand. The same build-floor guard failure also recurred in cycles 2466, 2508 and 2583 across three waves with no brake.
title: A shared fault across lanes engages the brake mid-wave and routes the blocker to the console
